name: GO Classes CS Test Series 2026 | Mixed Subjects | Full Length Test 1

question.text:
Assume the specifications

  • $F(x,y) : x$ is the father of $y$
  • $M(x,y) : x$ is the mother of $y.$

Which of the formulas in predicate logic below express the sentence 'Everybody has a mother'?

  1. $\exists x \forall y M(x, y)$
  2. $\exists y \forall x M(x, y)$
  3. $\forall x \exists y M(x, y)$
  4. $\forall y \exists x M(x, y)$

Let $\text{A}$ be an $n \times n$ matrix. Its only eigenvalues are $1,2,3,4,5$, possibly with multiplicities.

What is the nullity of the matrix $\text{A + I}_n,$ where $\text{I}_n$ is the $n \times n$ identity matrix?

  1. $0$
  2. $1$
  3. $n-1$
  4. $n-5$

Let $\mathbf{x}=\left[\begin{array}{c}1 \\ -2 \\ 5\end{array}\right]$ and $\mathbf{v}=\left[\begin{array}{c}-7 \\ 4 \\ 2\end{array}\right]$. Which of the following statements must be true?

  1. $A=\left[\begin{array}{ccc}-7 & 0 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]$ is of rank 1 such that $A \mathbf{x}=\mathbf{v}$.
  2. $A=\left[\begin{array}{ccc}-7 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 0\end{array}\right]$ is of rank 2 such that $A \mathbf{x}=\mathbf{v}$.
  3. $A=\left[\begin{array}{ccc}-7 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 / 5\end{array}\right]$ is of rank 3 such that $A \mathbf{x}=\mathbf{v}$.
  1. Only I
  2. Only II
  3. I, II
  4. All of them
What is the order of smallest non-cyclic group?

Consider the following scenario:
A box contains three coins: two regular coins and one fake two-headed coin, which always lands heads up.
If you randomly pick a coin from the box and toss it, what is the probability that it lands heads up?

  1. $1 / 2$
  2. $2 / 3$
  3. $1 / 3$
  4. $3 / 4$
The number of partitions of the set $\text{X} = \{a, b, c, d\}$ with “$a$” and “$b$” in the same block is ________

A matrix $A$ can be row reduced to the following echelon form
$$
\left[\begin{array}{lllll}
1 & 1 & 3 & 2 & 1 \\
0 & 1 & 2 & 1 & 3 \\
0 & 0 & 0 & a & b \\
0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & c
\end{array}\right]
$$
Depending on the values of the constants $a, b$ and $c$ the rank of $A$

  1. must be $2$
  2. must be $3$
  3. must be $4$
  4. can be $2, 3 \;\text{or}\; 4$

Let $\text{A}$ be any set.
The following are the definitions of Irreflexive and Asymmetric Relations :

  1. A binary relation $\text{R}$ on a set $\mathcal{A}$ is irreflexive iff $(x, x) \notin \text{R}$ for all $x \in \mathcal{A}$.
  2. A binary relation $\text{R}$ on a set $\mathcal{A}$ is asymmetric iff whenever $(x, y) \in \text{R}$, then $(y, x) \notin \text{R}$.

We define a "strict order relation" as follows :
A binary relation $\text{R}$ on a set $\text{A}$ is a strict order on $\text{A}$ iff $\text{R}$ is irreflexive and transitive.
Which of the following is/are true?

  1. Every strict order is asymmetric.
  2. Every strict order is total order relation.
  3. Every strict order is antisymmetric.
  4. Every relation which is both Irreflexive and Asymmetric, is strict order.

Let $\mathrm{G}$ be a finite group. Let "$1$" denote the identity element of $\text{G}.$ If $g$ is an element of a finite group $\mathrm{G},$ then the order of $g$ is the smallest positive integer $n$ such that $g^ n=1$, and it is denoted $o(g)=n$. The order of group $\mathrm{G}$ is denoted by $o(\mathrm{G})$ or $|\mathrm{G}|.$

Which of the following statements is necessarily true?

  1. If $g^ m=1,$ for some $g \in \mathrm{G},$ then $o(g) \mid m$.
  2. If $g^ m=1,$ for some $g \in \mathrm{G},$ then $o(g)=m$.
  3. If $g^ m=1,$ for some $\mathrm{g} \in \mathrm{G},$ then $m \mid o(\mathrm{g})$.
  4. If $g^ m=1,$ for some $g \in \mathrm{G},$ then $m \mid o(\mathrm{G})$.

A $k$-ary tree is a tree in which every node has at most $k$ children. In a $k$-ary tree with $n$ nodes and height $h,$ which of the following is an upper bound for the maximum number of leaves as a function of $h, k$, and $n?$ (height of the tree is the number of edges in the longest path from root to some leaf)

  1. $\log_k n$
  2. $n / \log _{k}(n)$
  3. $k^h$
  4. $h^k$
Let $\mathrm{G}$ be a non-cyclic group of order $57 .$ Then the number of elements of order $5$ in $\mathrm{G}$ is _______

You ask your neighbor to water a sickly plant while you are on vacation. Without water, the plant will die with a probability $0.8.$ With water, it will die with a probability $0.15.$ You are $90$ percent certain the neighbor will remember to water the plant.
What is the probability that the plant will be alive when you return?

  1. $0.85$
  2. $0.79$
  3. $0.90$
  4. $0.63$

Which of the following formulas is a formalization of the sentence: "Every connected and circuit-free graph is a tree". Where cir( $\mathrm{x})$ means " $\mathrm{x}$ has circuit"

  1. $\forall \mathrm{x}[(\operatorname{conn}(\mathrm{x}) \wedge \neg \operatorname{cir}(\mathrm{x})) \rightarrow \operatorname{tree}(\mathrm{x})]$
  2. $\neg \exists x[(\operatorname{conn}(\mathrm{x}) \wedge \neg \operatorname{cir}(\mathrm{x})) \wedge \neg \operatorname{tree}(\mathrm{x})]$
  3. $\forall \mathrm{x}[(\operatorname{conn}(\mathrm{x}) \wedge \neg \operatorname{cir}(\mathrm{x})) \wedge \operatorname{tree}(\mathrm{x})]$
  4. $\forall \mathrm{x}[(\operatorname{conn}(\mathrm{x}) \wedge \operatorname{cir}(\mathrm{x})) \rightarrow \operatorname{tree}(\mathrm{x})]$

Suppose a digital communications channel has a probability of bit error of $p$, where all errors are independent of each other. If you transmit $N$ bits, what's the probability that exactly $k$ bits are received incorrectly?

  1. $\left(\begin{array}{c}N \\ N-k\end{array}\right) p^{N-k}(1-p)^k$
  2. $p^{k-1}(1-p)$
  3. $(1-p)^{k-1} p$
  4. $\left(\begin{array}{c}N \\ k\end{array}\right) p^k(1-p)^{N-k}$
The number of elements which do not have complements in the above lattices is __________

A parallel system functions whenever at least one of its components works. Consider a parallel system of $n$ components and suppose that each component works with probability $p$ independently.
What is the probability the system is functioning?

  1. $(1-p)^n$
  2. $p^n$
  3. $1-(1-p)^n$
  4. $1-p^n$

Which of the following statements is TRUE?

  1. For all sets $\text{A, B}, $ and $\text{C, A - (B - C) = (A - B) - C}$.
  2. For all sets $\text{A, B}, $ and $\text{C, (A - B)} \cap \text{(C - B) = (A} \cap \text{C)- B}$.
  3. For all sets $\text{A, B}, $ and $\text{C, (A - B)} \cap \text{(C - B) = A - (B} \cup \text{C)}$.
  4. For all sets $\text{A, B}, $ and $\text{C},$ if $\text{A} \cap \text{C = B} \cap \text{C}$ then $\text{A = B}$.

Consider the statement form $\mathrm{S}:$
$$
p \vee(\sim p \wedge q) \Rightarrow \sim q .
$$
Which of the following is true?

  1. $\text{S}$ is a tautology
  2. $\text{S}$ is a Contradiction
  3. $\text{S}$ is a Contingency
  4. Antecedent of $\text{S}$ is equivalent to consequent of $\text{S}$

Let $A$ and $B$ are two events not necessarily independent.
$$
\begin{aligned}
& P(A, B)=0.15 \\
& P\left(A^c, B^c\right)=0.45 \\
& P(A)=0.6
\end{aligned}
$$
What is the probability of $P\left(A^c, B\right)?$
Find the number of positive integers $n \in N$, such that $1 \leq n \leq 1000$, which are not divisible by either $4,10$ or $15 .$

Let $A, B$ be two predicate logic formulas. We say that “$A \models B$” (which means that “$A$ infers $B$”) iff for all interpretations in which $A$ is true, $B$ is also true.
So, “$A \models B$” iff “$A \rightarrow B$” is valid.

Which of the following inferences are valid in predicate logic?

  1. $\forall x (P(x) \vee Q(x)) \models \forall x P(x) \vee \forall x Q(x)$
  2. $\forall x (P(x) \rightarrow Q(x)) \models \forall x P(x) \rightarrow \forall x Q(x)$
  3. $\forall x P(x) \rightarrow \forall x Q(x) \models \forall x (P(x) \rightarrow Q(x))$
  4. $\neg \forall x (P(x) \wedge Q(x)) \models \exists x \neg P(x) \wedge \exists x \neg Q(x)$

Consider the matrix $A=\left[\begin{array}{rrrr}1 & 3 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 4 & -2\end{array}\right]$ whose row echelon form is $\left[\begin{array}{llll}1 & 0 & a & b \\ 0 & 1 & c & d\end{array}\right]$. Find $a+b+c+d$ :

  1. $-7$
  2. $-4$
  3. $-3$
  4. $-1$

Let $X$ be a random variable that takes values from $0$ to $9$ with equal probability $1 / 10$.

Let $Z$ be a random variable $Z=(5 \bmod (X+1))$.

Find $P(Z=1)?$

  1. $1 / 10$
  2. $2 / 10$
  3. $5 / 10$
  4. $0$

Let $Z=3 X-Y-5$, where $X$ and $Y$ are independent random variables with $\operatorname{Var}(X)=1$ and $\operatorname{Var}(Y)=2$. What is $\operatorname{Var}(Z)?$

  1. $4$
  2. $7$
  3. $11$
  4. None of the above.

Consider now a refined probabilistic model with $n=2$ questions. For $i \in\{1,2\}$, let $X_i$ be an indicator random variable which is $1$ iff question $i$ is answered correctly by the student. We know $\mathbf{P}\left[X_1=1 \mid X_2=0\right]=0.4, \mathbf{P}\left[X_2=1 \mid X_1=1\right]=0.8$ and $\mathbf{P}\left[X_1=1\right]=0.5$

Compute the $P\left[X_2=1 \mid X_1=0\right]$

A full binary tree is a rooted tree in which every internal node has exactly two children. How many internal nodes are there in a full binary tree with $500$ leaves?

  1. $250$
  2. $499$
  3. $500$
  4. $501$

Number of Linearly independent eigenvectors corresponding to the matrix
$$
\left(\begin{array}{ccc}
1 & 0 & 0 \\
-2 & 2 & -1 \\
4 & 0 & 3 \\
\end{array}\right)
$$

Suppose $A=\left[\begin{array}{llll}\mathbf{a}_1 & \mathbf{a}_2 & \cdots & \mathbf{a}_n\end{array}\right]$ is an $n \times n$ invertible matrix, and $\mathbf{b}$ is a non-zero vector in $\mathbb{R}^n$. Which of the following statements is / are true?

  1. $\mathbf{b}$ is a linear combination of $\left\{\mathbf{a}_1, \mathbf{a}_2, \ldots, \mathbf{a}_n\right\}$.
  2. The determinant of $A$ is nonzero.
  3. $\operatorname{rank} A=n$.
  4. If $A \mathbf{b}=\lambda \mathbf{b}$ for some constant $\lambda$, then $\lambda \neq 0$.

An Euler circuit of an undirected graph is a circuit in which each edge of the graph appears exactly once. Which of the following undirected graphs must have an Euler circuit?

  1. A complete graph with $12$ vertices
  2. A complete graph with $13$ vertices
  3. A tree with $13$ vertices
  1. I only
  2. II only
  3. III only
  4. I and II Only

Let $\mathcal{P}(A)$ denote the power set of $\text{A}.$ If $\mathcal{P}(\text{A}) \subseteq \text{B}$ then

  1. $2^{|\text{A}|} \leq|\text{B}|$
  2. $2^{|\text{A}|} \geq|\text{B}|$
  3. $2|\text{A}|<|\text{B}|$
  4. $|\text{A}|+2 \leq|\text{B}|$

Consider the matrix $\mathbf{A} \in \mathbb{R}^{2 \times 2}$, which takes a vector $\vec{v}=\left[\begin{array}{l}x \\ y\end{array}\right]$ and scales its $y$ component by $2,$ but leaves the $x$ component unchanged. In other words, $\mathbf{A}\left[\begin{array}{l}x \\ y\end{array}\right]=\left[\begin{array}{c}x \\ 2 y\end{array}\right]$.

What are the eigenvalues of $\mathbf{A}?$

  1. $1,0$
  2. $2,0$
  3. $1,2$
  4. $-1,2$
The number of different Total order relations on a set of $7$ elements is _______

Suppose $\text{Y}$ has a discrete distribution with pmf given by
$$
\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|}
\hline y & 0 & 1 & 2 & 3\\
\hline p_\textsf{Y}(y) & 1 / 2 & 1 / 4 & 1 / 8 & 1 / 8\\
\hline
\end{array}$$
Calculate $\text{E}\left[(\text{Y}-1)^2\right]?$

  1. $1 / 4$
  2. $1 / 8$
  3. $9 / 8$
  4. $3 / 4$

Consider a $5 \times 6$ rectangular grid as depicted in Figure $1.$ A staircase walk is a path in the grid which moves only right or up.

What is the total number of staircase walks from $\text{A}$ to $\text{B}$ that may or may not pass through the point $\text{P?}$

Suppose you wish to determine whether a set of vectors $\left\{\mathbf{v}_1, \mathbf{v}_2, \mathbf{v}_3, \mathbf{v}_4\right\}$ is linearly independent. You form the matrix $A=\left[\begin{array}{llll}\mathbf{v}_1 & \mathbf{v}_2 & \mathbf{v}_3 & \mathbf{v}_4\end{array}\right]$ and you calculate its reduced row echelon form, $R=\left[\begin{array}{llll}1 & 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]$. You now decide to write $\mathbf{v}_2$ as a linear combination of $\mathbf{v}_1, \mathbf{v}_3$, and $\mathbf{v}_4$. Which is /are correct linear combination?

  1. $\mathbf{v}_2=\mathbf{v}_3-2 \mathbf{v}_4$
  2. $\mathbf{v}_2=-3 \mathbf{v}_3-\mathbf{v}_4$
  3. $\mathbf{v}_2=\mathbf{v}_4-3 \mathbf{v}_3$
  4. $\mathbf{v}_2=-\mathbf{v}_1+\mathbf{v}_4$

Suppose that $A$ is $n \times m$. Which of the following statements must be true?

  1. If $\operatorname{Rank}(A)=n$ and $m>n$ (i.e., $m \geq n+1$ ), then the system $A \mathbf{x}=\mathbf{0}$ has infinitely many solutions.
  2. If $\operatorname{Rank}(A)=m$ and $m \leq n$, then $A \mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$ has a unique solution.
  3. If $\operatorname{Rank}(A)=m$ and $m \leq n$, then $A \mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$ has at most one solution.
  4. If $\operatorname{Rank}(A)=n$ and $m>n$, (i.e., $m \geq n+1$ ), then $A \mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$ has infinitely many solution.
  1. I, II, III
  2. II, IV
  3. I, III, IV
  4. I, II, IV

Which of the following propositional logic formulas is/are valid?

  1. $(p \rightarrow q) \wedge \neg q \rightarrow \neg p$
  2. $(p \rightarrow q) \rightarrow(p \rightarrow \neg q)$
  3. $(p \vee q \rightarrow \mathrm{r}) \vee p \vee q$
  4. $(p \vee q) \wedge(p \rightarrow r \wedge q) \wedge(q \rightarrow \neg r \wedge p)$

Let $n \in \mathrm{N}$,

Consider the following two combinatorial identities :

  1. $\left(\begin{array}{c}2 n \\2\\\end{array}\right)=2\left(\begin{array}{l}n\\2\\\end{array}\right)+n^2 .$
  2. $\left(\begin{array}{l}n\\0\\\end{array}\right)+2^1\left(\begin{array}{l}n\\1\\\end{array}\right)+2^2\left(\begin{array}{l}n\\2\\\end{array}\right)+\ldots+2^k\left(\begin{array}{l}n\\k\\\end{array}\right)+\ldots+2^n\left(\begin{array}{l}n\\n\\\end{array}\right)=3^n .$

Which of the above are correct?

  1. Only $1$
  2. Only $2$
  3. Both
  4. None

The power set $\mathcal{P}((\text{A} \times \text{B}) \cup(B \times \text{A}))$ has the same number of elements as the power set $\mathcal{P}((\text{A} \times \text{B}) \cup(\text{A} \times \text{B}))$ if and only if

  1. $\text{A = B}$
  2. $\text{A}=\emptyset$ or $\text{B}=\emptyset$
  3. $\text{B}=\emptyset$ or $\text{A = B}$
  4. $\text{A} = \emptyset$ or $\text{B} = \emptyset$ or $\text{A = B}$

Let $\text{A}=\left[\begin{array}{cc}
1 & -1 \\
0 & 2
\end{array}\right]$, and let $\text{B}$ be a $2 \times 3$ matrix. Suppose that the second row of $\text{(A B)}^\text{T}$ is $\mathbf{v}=[-1 \quad 3]$
Compute the second column of $\text{B}$.

  1. $
    \left[\begin{array}{c}
    -1\\
    3\\
    \end{array}\right]
    $
  2. $
    \left[\begin{array}{l}
    \frac{1}{2}\\
    \frac{3}{2}\\
    \end{array}\right]
    $
  3. $
    \left[\begin{array}{l}
    \frac{1}{3}\\
    1\\
    \end{array}\right]
    $
  4. $
    \left[\begin{array}{c}
    3\\
    -1\\
    \end{array}\right]
    $

Which of the following statements is/are True?

  1. $\{2,3,4\} \subseteq \text{A}$ implies that $2 \in \text{A}$ and $\{3,4\} \subseteq \text{A}.$
  2. $\{2,3,4\} \in \text{A}$ and $\{2,3\} \in \text{B}$ implies that $\{4\} \subseteq \text{A - B}.$
  3. $\text{A} \cap \text{B} \supseteq\{2,3,4\}$ implies that $\{2,3,4\} \subseteq \text{A}$ and $\{2,3,4\} \subseteq \text{B}.$
  4. $\text{A - B} \supseteq\{3,4\}$ and $\{1,2\} \subseteq \text{B}$ implies that $\{1,2,3,4\} \subseteq \text{A} \cup \text{B}.$

Let $[P(S), \supseteq]$ be a partial order relation defined on $P(S),$ where $S = \{1,2,3,4\}. P(S)$ is the set of all subsets of $S.$ Which of the following is the join of $\{1,2\}, \{3,4\}?$

  1. $\{3,4\}$
  2. $\{1,2,3,4\}$
  3. $\varnothing $
  4. $\{1,2\}$

For what value of $c$ are the vectors $\left(\begin{array}{c}-1 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{array}\right),\left(\begin{array}{l}2 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{array}\right)$ and $\left(\begin{array}{l}1 \\ 1 \\ c\end{array}\right)$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$ linearly dependent?

Let $\text{G}$ be a group. Let "$1$" denote the identity element of $\text{G}.$ Which of the following is/are true?

  1. if $a^{-1}=a$ for all $a \in \text{G}$, then $\text{G}$ is abelian.
  2. if for all $a, b, c \in \text{G}, a b=c a \Rightarrow b=c$, then $\text{G}$ is abelian
  3. If $(a * b)^{-1}=\left(b^{-1}\right) *\left(a^{-1}\right)$ for every $a, b \in \text{G},$,= then $\mathrm{G}$ is abelian.
  4. $(a b)^n=a^n b^n$ for all $a, b \in \text{G}$, $n \in Z$ if and only if $\text{G}$ is abelian.
The set $\{1, 2, 3, \dots , n - 1\}$ is a group under multiplication modulo $n.$ Then the smallest value of $n$ between $20$ and $30$ is $(20, 30$ included $)\;$ _______

Anne and Betty go fishing. Assume they catch fish independently and that each has a probability $0 < p < 1$ of catching no fish. Let $A$ be the event that Anne catches no fish and $B$ be the event that Betty catches no fish. 

Find the conditional probability that Anne catches no fish given that at least one of them catches no fish i.e. $P(A \mid(A \cup B))$.

  1. $1 /(1-p)$
  2. $1 /(2-p)$
  3. $1 / p$
  4. None of these

Given two Boolean random variables, $A$ and $B$, where $P(A)=1 / 2, \quad P(B)=1 / 3,$ and $\mathrm{P}(A \mid \neg B)=1 / 4$, what is $\mathrm{P}(A \mid B)?$

  1. $1 / 6$
  2. $1 / 4$
  3. $3 / 4$
  4. $1$

For a connected, undirected graph $\text{G = (V, E)},$ which of the following must be true?

  1. $\sum_{v \in \text{V}}$ degree $(\mathrm{v})$ is even.
  2. $|\mathrm{E}| \geq|\mathrm{V}|-1$
  3. $\mathrm{G}$ has at least one vertex with degree $1.$
  1. I only
  2. I, II only
  3. I, III only
  4. I, II, III

We have a circuit with two devices between points $a$ and $b$. The circuit will work if there is at least one path between $a$ and $b$. The probability of each device working is shown on the graph, and we assume independent device failures. What is the probability of the circuit functioning correctly?

  1. $0.905$
  2. $0.998$
  3. $0.915$
  4. $0.940$

Let $(L, \#)$ be a lattice, where $\#$ is some partial order relation defined on the base set $L$. Let $x,y,z \in L.$ Which of the following is/are necessarily true?

  1. $x \vee y = y \vee x$
  2. $x \vee (x \wedge y) = x$
  3. $x \vee (y \wedge z) = (x \vee y) \wedge (x \vee z)$
  4. $x \wedge (x \vee y) = x$

Let $\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}$ denote events in a sample space $\mathrm{S}$ and let $\mathrm{P}(.)$ denote a probability measure on $\mathrm{S}$. Which of the following is/are TRUE?

  1. If $P(A \mid B)=P(A)$ then $P(B \mid A)=P(B)$.
  2. If $P(A) \leq P(B)$ then $A \subset B$.
  3. If $A \subset B$ then $P(A) \leq P(B)$
  4. $P\left(A \mid B^{\prime}\right)=1-P(A \mid B)$

A graph is said to be $2$-colourable if each vertex can be coloured either red or blue and no two vertices of the same colour are connected by an edge. If some graph is not $2$-colorable, then we can reduce it to become $2$-colorable by deleting some edges. We are given any simple graph with $101$ nodes. $k$ is the least required number of edges we have to delete in order to make this graph $2$-colorable (Eg: $k=0$ for a graph which is already $2$-colorable).
The minimum value for ' $k$ ' to reach the worst case is _______

Which of the following statements is true for every matrix $\text{M}$ with $m$ rows and $n$ columns, where $m<n?$

  1. The system $\text{M} \mathbf{x}=\mathbf{0}$ has no solution.
  2. The system $\text{M} \mathbf{x}=\mathbf{0}$ has infinitely many solutions.
  3. For every $\mathbf{b}$ in $\mathbb{R}^m$, the system $\text{M} \mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$ has infinitely many solutions.
  4. For some $\mathbf{b}$ in $\mathbb{R}^m$, the system $\text{M} \mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$ has a unique solution.

Given a graph $\mathrm{G}$ is a connected planar simple graph with ' $e$ ' edges and ' $v$ ' vertices, with $v \geq 3$ and if all cycles in $\text{G}$ have length $\geq 4$, then which of the following relations hold always?
 

  1. $e \leq 2 v-4$
  2. $e \leq 2 v-2$
  3. $e \leq 3 v-4$
  4. None of these

Let $f: \text{X} \rightarrow \text{Y}$ and $g: \text{Y} \rightarrow \text{Z}.$ Let $h=g \circ f: \text{X} \rightarrow \text{Z}.$ Suppose $g$ is one-to-one and onto. Which of the following is FALSE?

  1. If $f$ is one-to-one then $h$ is one-to-one and onto.
  2. If $f$ is not onto then $h$ is not onto.
  3. If $f$ is not one-to-one then $h$ is not one-to-one.
  4. If $f$ is one-to-one then $h$ is one-to-one.

Let $\text{G}=\langle\{e, a, b, c, d\}, *\rangle$ be a group with the following Cayley table partially completed.
$$\begin{array}{|l|l|l|l|l|l|}
\hline \ast & e & a & b & c & d \\
\hline e & e & a & b & c & d \\
\hline a & a & & e & b & \\
\hline b & b & & & & \\
\hline c & c & & & & \\
\hline d & d & & & & \\
\hline
\end{array}$$
Which of the following is/are true for the given group $\text{G}?$

  1. $\text{G}$ is a cyclic group.
  2. $\mathrm{G}$ is abelian.
  3. The number of generators in $\mathrm{G}$ is $4.$
  4. The order of $d$ is $2.$

Consider the following augmented matrix where $\ast$ can be any value that is not $0$ and not $1:$
$$
\left[\begin{array}{llll|l}
1 & \ast & \ast & \ast & \ast \\
0 & 0 & \ast & \ast & \ast \\
0 & 0 & \ast & \ast & \ast \\
0 & 0 & 1 & \ast & \ast
\end{array}\right]
$$
The system of linear equations represented:

  1. has a unique solution
  2. has no unique solution
  3. has infinite solutions
  4. has no solutions

Find an equation relating $a, b$ and $c$ so that the linear system
$$
\begin{aligned}
x+2 y-3 z & =a \\
x-y+8 z & =b \\
-6 x-3 y-15 z & =c
